selfVerdict: Works as a direction, with one honest weakness. What lands: it reads as a ruled public-information bulletin, not a dashboard or a template. A 3px ink rule, fixed-order rows (area, sentence, against-normal word, confidence), tinted blue/rust anomaly cells and one open row whose numbers sit on an illustrative normal-range bar carry the mechanism; the same title-left/entry-right grid runs down the page (synopsis on a white band, 'normal' as a two-tone statement). Badge, QR, price and the sticky bar are in-world (issue row, bulletin footer rule), no stars, no cards, no kicker, no split hero. Weaknesses: the palette is overcast grey, white and ink, so at thumbnail size it is a very well-set Nordic information page rather than an unmistakable world; the strongest identity is typographic discipline and the two tints. The product's own dark UI appears nowhere in these two screens (screenshots come at entry 7 in this order), so the sketch undersells the app; the Quick Answer is a 120-word block that fills the second screen; there is dead space top-right beside the H1. If the owner likes it, the next build should move one screenshot panel up, or commit harder to colour. It is the most familiar of the three (recovery apps already say readiness/forecast), so the craft has to stay in the typography.
